title: Inorder Successor in BST
description:
Given the `root` of a binary search tree (BST) and a node `p` in it, return the **inorder successor** of that node in the BST. If the given node has no inorder successor in the tree, return `null`.

The **successor** of a node `p` is the node with the **smallest key strictly greater than `p.val`**.

In the test inputs, `p` is specified by its unique integer value; the judge locates the corresponding `TreeNode` reference inside `root` and passes that node reference to your method. You must return the existing `TreeNode` reference from the tree (or `null` if none exists) without modifying node values; the judge displays the returned node's value (or `null`).
constraints: 1 <= number of nodes in the tree <= 10^4
p is guaranteed to exist in the BST.
hints: Instead of traversing the entire tree in O(n), leverage the BST ordering property to search directly from the root in O(h) time.
Maintain a candidate successor initialized to null. At the current node, if p.val < curr.val, then curr is a valid candidate successor — record it and move left to look for a smaller one.
Otherwise (p.val >= curr.val), curr and its entire left subtree cannot be the successor, so move right.

examples.explanation: The inorder traversal is [1, 2, 3], so the successor of node 1 is node 2.
Node 6 is the maximum value in the BST, so it has no inorder successor (null).
Node 4 has no right child; its inorder successor is the lowest ancestor whose left subtree contains 4, which is node 5.

inputs.name: root
inputs.description: Level-order representation of a BST with unique values

inputs.name: p
inputs.description: Value of target node p inside the BST
